advertise_mode.description:
User-specified flag to indicate which mode to use for advertisement.
Valid values of this enum field are: 'DEFAULT', 'CUSTOM' Default value: "DEFAULT" Possible values: ["DEFAULT", "CUSTOM"]
advertise_mode.rationale: Chooses how routes are advertised (DEFAULT or CUSTOM). This is a routing design choice and neither value is insecure, so no policy is needed.

advertised_groups.description:
User-specified list of prefix groups to advertise in custom
mode, which currently supports the following option:

* 'ALL_SUBNETS': Advertises all of the router's own VPC subnets.
This excludes any routes learned for subnets that use VPC Network
Peering.


Note that this field can only be populated if advertiseMode is 'CUSTOM'
and overrides the list defined for the router (in the "bgp" message).
These groups are advertised in addition to any specified prefixes.
Leave this field blank to advertise no custom groups.
advertised_groups.rationale: Chooses which groups of subnets are advertised to the peer. What a team advertises to its own trusted router is a routing choice, not a security control.

advertised_route_priority.description:
The priority of routes advertised to this BGP peer.
Where there is more than one matching route of maximum
length, the routes with the lowest priority value win.
advertised_route_priority.rationale: Sets the priority of routes advertised to the peer. This only tunes traffic preference and does not affect security.

custom_learned_route_priority.description:
The user-defined custom learned route priority for a BGP session.
This value is applied to all custom learned route ranges for the session. You can choose a value
from 0 to 65335. If you don't provide a value, Google Cloud assigns a priority of 100 to the ranges.
custom_learned_route_priority.rationale: Sets the priority of routes learned from the peer. This only tunes traffic preference and does not affect security.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform is allowed to destroy the BGP peer. If the peer is deleted by accident, VPN/Interconnect routing goes down. A policy should require 'PREVENT' to block accidental destroys.

enable.description:
The status of the BGP peer connection. If set to false, any active session
with the peer is terminated and all associated routing information is removed.
If set to true, the peer connection can be established with routing information.
The default is true.
enable.rationale: Turns the BGP session on or off. This is an operational switch and neither value is insecure.

enable_ipv4.description: Enable IPv4 traffic over BGP Peer. It is enabled by default if the peerIpAddress is version 4.
enable_ipv4.rationale: Turns IPv4 traffic on or off for the session. This is a functional choice, not a security control.

enable_ipv6.description: Enable IPv6 traffic over BGP Peer. If not specified, it is disabled by default.
enable_ipv6.rationale: Turns IPv6 traffic on or off for the session. This is a functional choice, not a security control.

export_policies.description:
routers.list of export policies applied to this peer, in the order they must be evaluated. 
The name must correspond to an existing policy that has ROUTE_POLICY_TYPE_EXPORT type.
export_policies.rationale: Names of existing export route policies to apply. This is a reference to another resource; we secure the route policy itself, not the name pointing to it.

import_policies.description:
routers.list of import policies applied to this peer, in the order they must be evaluated. 
The name must correspond to an existing policy that has ROUTE_POLICY_TYPE_IMPORT type.
import_policies.rationale: Names of existing import route policies to apply. This is a reference to another resource; we secure the route policy itself, not the name pointing to it.

interface.description: Name of the interface the BGP peer is associated with.
interface.rationale: Name of the router interface this peer uses. This is just a reference, not a security control.

ip_address.description:
IP address of the interface inside Google Cloud Platform.
Only IPv4 is supported.
ip_address.rationale: IP address of the interface inside Google Cloud. IP addressing is a team decision and a generic policy cannot check it.

ipv4_nexthop_address.description: IPv4 address of the interface inside Google Cloud Platform.
ipv4_nexthop_address.rationale: IPv4 next-hop address inside Google Cloud. IP addressing is a team decision and a generic policy cannot check it.

ipv6_nexthop_address.description:
IPv6 address of the interface inside Google Cloud Platform.
The address must be in the range 2600:2d00:0:2::/64 or 2600:2d00:0:3::/64.
If you do not specify the next hop addresses, Google Cloud automatically
assigns unused addresses from the 2600:2d00:0:2::/64 or 2600:2d00:0:3::/64 range for you.
ipv6_nexthop_address.rationale: IPv6 next-hop address inside Google Cloud. IP addressing is a team decision and a generic policy cannot check it.

name.description:
Name of this BGP peer. The name must be 1-63 characters long,
and comply with RFC1035. Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters
long and match the regular expression '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?' which
means the first character must be a lowercase letter, and all
following characters must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit,
except the last character, which cannot be a dash.
name.rationale: Name of the BGP peer. A name does not affect the security of the resource or its data.

peer_asn.description:
Peer BGP Autonomous System Number (ASN).
Each BGP interface may use a different value.
peer_asn.rationale: The peer network's BGP AS number. It identifies the team's own peer, and a generic policy cannot check it without hardcoding team-specific values.

peer_ip_address.description:
IP address of the BGP interface outside Google Cloud Platform.
Only IPv4 is supported. Required if 'ip_address' is set.
peer_ip_address.rationale: IP address of the peer's BGP interface. IP addressing is a team decision and a generic policy cannot check it.

peer_ipv4_nexthop_address.description: IPv4 address of the BGP interface outside Google Cloud Platform.
peer_ipv4_nexthop_address.rationale: IPv4 next-hop address on the peer side. IP addressing is a team decision and a generic policy cannot check it.

peer_ipv6_nexthop_address.description:
IPv6 address of the BGP interface outside Google Cloud Platform.
The address must be in the range 2600:2d00:0:2::/64 or 2600:2d00:0:3::/64.
If you do not specify the next hop addresses, Google Cloud automatically
assigns unused addresses from the 2600:2d00:0:2::/64 or 2600:2d00:0:3::/64 range for you.
peer_ipv6_nexthop_address.rationale: IPv6 next-hop address on the peer side. IP addressing is a team decision and a generic policy cannot check it.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: The project the resource belongs to. This is just a reference, not a security control.

region.description:
Region where the router and BgpPeer reside.
If it is not provided, the provider region is used.
region.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

router.description: The name of the Cloud Router in which this BgpPeer will be configured.
router.rationale: Name of the Cloud Router this peer is created on. This is just a reference, not a security control.

router_appliance_instance.description:
The URI of the VM instance that is used as third-party router appliances
such as Next Gen Firewalls, Virtual Routers, or Router Appliances.
The VM instance must be located in zones contained in the same region as
this Cloud Router. The VM instance is the peer side of the BGP session.
router_appliance_instance.rationale: Link to the VM used as the router appliance. This is a reference to another resource, not a security control.

zero_advertised_route_priority.rationale: Forces the advertised route priority to 0. This only tunes traffic preference and does not affect security.

zero_custom_learned_route_priority.rationale: Forces the learned route priority to 0. This only tunes traffic preference and does not affect security.

advertised_ip_ranges.description:
User-specified list of individual IP ranges to advertise in
custom mode. This field can only be populated if advertiseMode
is 'CUSTOM' and is advertised to all peers of the router. These IP
ranges will be advertised in addition to any specified groups.
Leave this field blank to advertise no custom IP ranges.

advertised_ip_ranges.description.description: User-specified description for the IP range.
advertised_ip_ranges.description.rationale: A text description of the IP range. Descriptions have no security impact.

advertised_ip_ranges.range.description:
The IP range to advertise. The value must be a
CIDR-formatted string.
advertised_ip_ranges.range.rationale: The IP range advertised to the peer. IP ranges are team addressing decisions; network protection comes from firewall rules, not from restricting range values.

bfd.description: BFD configuration for the BGP peering.

bfd.min_receive_interval.description:
The minimum interval, in milliseconds, between BFD control packets
received from the peer router. The actual value is negotiated
between the two routers and is equal to the greater of this value
and the transmit interval of the other router. If set, this value
must be between 1000 and 30000.
bfd.min_receive_interval.rationale: BFD timer controlling how fast link failures are detected. This is availability tuning, not a security control.

bfd.min_transmit_interval.description:
The minimum interval, in milliseconds, between BFD control packets
transmitted to the peer router. The actual value is negotiated
between the two routers and is equal to the greater of this value
and the corresponding receive interval of the other router. If set,
this value must be between 1000 and 30000.
bfd.min_transmit_interval.rationale: BFD timer controlling how fast link failures are detected. This is availability tuning, not a security control.

bfd.multiplier.description:
The number of consecutive BFD packets that must be missed before
BFD declares that a peer is unavailable. If set, the value must
be a value between 5 and 16.
bfd.multiplier.rationale: How many missed BFD packets mark the peer as down. This is availability tuning, not a security control.

bfd.session_initialization_mode.description:
The BFD session initialization mode for this BGP peer.
If set to 'ACTIVE', the Cloud Router will initiate the BFD session
for this BGP peer. If set to 'PASSIVE', the Cloud Router will wait
for the peer router to initiate the BFD session for this BGP peer.
If set to 'DISABLED', BFD is disabled for this BGP peer. Possible values: ["ACTIVE", "DISABLED", "PASSIVE"]
bfd.session_initialization_mode.rationale: Chooses how the BFD session starts (ACTIVE, PASSIVE or DISABLED). BFD only detects link failures, so this is availability tuning, not a security control.

custom_learned_ip_ranges.description:
The custom learned route IP address range. Must be a valid CIDR-formatted prefix. If an 
IP address is provided without a subnet mask, it is interpreted as, for IPv4, a /32 singular IP address range, and, for IPv6, /128.

custom_learned_ip_ranges.range.description:
The IP range to learn. The value must be a
CIDR-formatted string.
custom_learned_ip_ranges.range.rationale: The IP range learned from the peer. IP ranges are team addressing decisions; network protection comes from firewall rules, not from restricting range values.

md5_authentication_key.description:
Present if MD5 authentication is enabled for the peering. Must be the name
of one of the entries in the Router.md5_authentication_keys. The field must comply with RFC1035.

md5_authentication_key.key.rationale: The secret key value itself. A generic policy cannot validate a secret value and must never hardcode or match real key material.

md5_authentication_key.name.description:
[REQUIRED] Name used to identify the key.
Must be unique within a router. Must be referenced by exactly one bgpPeer. Must comply with RFC1035.
md5_authentication_key.name.rationale: Identifies the MD5 key that authenticates the BGP session. Without authentication the session can be spoofed and false routes injected. A policy should require this to be set (non-empty) so every peer uses authenticated BGP, without pinning any specific key name.
